title: Full rule×rule attractor-dominance map (n=4): a strict partial order
question: For all ordered pairs of {30,110,105,150}, does 2-phase (A then B) lock to A's attractor or escape to B's — and does the dominance relation form a partial order?
engine: pure hexa-lang. n=4 ECA. phase-1 ruleA ×20, phase-2 ruleB ×20; outcome by Manhattan distance of final histogram to A-baseline (lock) vs B-baseline (escape).

partial_order.105: BOTTOM — incomparable to 150 (each holds its own attractor); loses to 30, 110
partial_order.consistency: every pair is order-consistent across both orderings; 105∥150 are mutually incomparable (each phase-1 holds its own disjoint bijection attractor)

falsifier_eval.F336_1_PARTIAL_ORDER: PASS — the 12 outcomes form a consistent strict partial order 110 > 30 > {105,150}; no cyclic (A>B>C>A) inconsistency
falsifier_eval.F336_2_NOT_ALL_PHASE1: PASS — A_locks=7, B_wins=5; phase-1 does NOT trivially always win, so the order is non-trivial
falsifier_eval.F336_3_NOT_ALL_PHASE2: PASS — B does not always win either
falsifier_eval.F336_4_NO_MIXED: PASS — mixed=0; every pair resolves cleanly to lock-or-escape (no partial/ambiguous attractors at n=4)

verdict_derived: 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL — attractor dominance forms a clean STRICT PARTIAL ORDER: rule110 (universal class IV) dominates all others, rule30 (chaotic class III) dominates the two bijection rules, and rules 105/150 are mutually INCOMPARABLE (each holds its own disjoint attractor, neither can lock the other out). mixed=0 means every ordered pair resolves cleanly. This unifies the session's attractor findings: H_332 (dominance exists), H_335 (dominance is permanent), H_336 (dominance is a partial order with universal > chaotic > bijection). The order also matches the H_334 n-oscillation reading: rule110 and rule30 are the two top-of-order rules that trade the longest-cycle slot across n.
structural_vs_dynamical: DYNAMICAL kernel; the discovery is a global ordering relation over rules, not a single-rule property. The universal > chaotic > bijection hierarchy is a clean dynamical-systems result on ECA attractor basins.
honest_limits: n=4; the partial order may not be preserved at larger n (H_334 shows attractor structure is n-dependent — 110/30 already trade ranks)
4 rules / 12 ordered pairs; a wider rule set could introduce cycles (non-transitive dominance) that would break the partial-order claim
20+20 phase lengths; H_335 showed lock is T-permanent for the 110→30 pair, but other pairs were not phase-swept here
Final-state marginal metric; trajectory-level dominance could differ
discovery_note: attractor dominance = strict partial order (110 > 30 > {105∥150}). universal class IV가 top, chaotic class III가 middle, bijection이 bottom + 서로 incomparable. 세션 attractor arc(H_332 존재 → H_335 영구 → H_336 순서) 통합.
